findings.finding: `reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")` called without `errors=` resets the stream's error handler to `strict`. `sys.stderr` defaults to `backslashreplace`, so after this change on Windows, writing an unencodable character such as a lone surrogate to stderr raises instead of being escaped. A traceback or log message can then itself crash. The plan's stdio test checks only that the encoding reads `utf-8`, not that stderr keeps its error handler.

findings.finding: Treating a `UnicodeDecodeError` in `_read_existing_commit` as 'no baked SHA' throws away a valid SHA. In a stale cp1252 `_build_info.py`, only the em dash in the docstring is non-ASCII; the `COMMIT = '<sha>'` line is ASCII and could still be read. Precedence step 2 exists to preserve the baked SHA in a tree with no git (the module docstring says the hook refuses to lose provenance silently). Reading with `errors="replace"` turns the bad byte into U+FFFD inside the docstring, the file still parses with ast, and the SHA is recovered. That handles this edge case better than falling through to git, or to None when there is no `.git`.

"`_read_existing_commit` (`:65`) treats `UnicodeDecodeError` as 'no baked SHA'" — no encoding stated for the read
"Failing tests get `encoding="utf-8"`" — only failing ones
findings.finding: The PLW1514 criterion is a one-time check on the merged tree. No step adds the rule to the ruff config or CI, and the command excludes `hatch_build.py` and `tests/`. Those are the two places this bug class originated, and the hatch read in `_read_existing_commit` is not even stated to pass `encoding="utf-8"`.
findings.location: Approach — PLW1514 bullet and hatch_build bullet / AC 3
scenarios: A new `Path.write_text(...)` without encoding is added to `src/` or `hatch_build.py` next month. CI stays green on Linux and the Windows sweep regresses.
findings.suggested_fix: In the ruff config, add `PLW1514` to the selected rules, with `preview = true` and `explicit-preview-rules = true` so that only explicitly listed preview rules are enabled. Change the AC command to `ruff check --preview --select PLW1514 hatch_build.py src scripts`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the hook's behaviour after the UnicodeDecodeError fallback when `_build_commit` cannot reach git, and emit a build-time warning when the stale file is discarded.
evidence: "treats `UnicodeDecodeError` as 'no baked SHA'"
findings.finding: When `_read_existing_commit` hits `UnicodeDecodeError` it silently returns 'no baked SHA'. The plan does not say what the hook then does when git is unavailable, as in an sdist build. It also does not say whether the fallback is logged.
findings.location: Approach — hatch_build bullet
scenarios: An sdist built on Windows before the fix carries a cp1252 `_build_info.py` and is rebuilt without git. Provenance is silently dropped.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the terminal disposition of the baked-SHA → git fallback when both are unavailable (fail the build vs record 'unknown') and that the stale file is rewritten as UTF-8.
evidence: "`_read_existing_commit` (`:65`) treats `UnicodeDecodeError` as \"no baked SHA\"."
Testing: "edge: a cp1252 stale `_build_info.py` yields no baked SHA instead of raising." (covers only the first arm)
findings.finding: The plan alters exception handling in `_read_existing_commit` so that UnicodeDecodeError means "no baked SHA". It does not state the resulting disposition: what the build ends up recording when the baked SHA is unreadable and `_build_commit`'s git call is also unavailable (e.g. an sdist build). Nor does it say whether the stale cp1252 file is then rewritten in UTF-8. The fallback chain (baked SHA → git) has no stated terminal outcome.
findings.location: Approach — `hatch_build.py` bullet
scenarios: An sdist built from a tree with a stale cp1252 `_build_info.py` and no git: build provenance silently becomes empty or unknown instead of failing loudly or keeping the SHA.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that PLW1514 does not cover subprocess text-mode pipes, and either widen the subprocess fix/gate beyond the five CLI-consumer modules or explicitly scope the remaining `text=True` sites out (with a follow-up ticket).
evidence: Ruff docs (retrieved): 'unspecified-encoding (PLW1514). Preview ... Derived from the Pylint linter' — the description covers `open` in text mode; nothing in the retrieved docs or pylint W1514 docs mentions subprocess.

Repo search `text=True` under src/rebar returns about 90 subprocess sites outside the five CLI-consumer modules, e.g. src/rebar/_commands/verify_commit.py:142 (`git show -s --format=%B` — commit messages can be non-ASCII), src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py:275, src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:338, src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:366.
Plan only fixes subprocess encoding in 'these five modules'.
findings.finding: The plan treats `ruff check --preview --select PLW1514 src scripts` as the completeness gate for locale-default text I/O. PLW1514 (unspecified-encoding, derived from pylint W1514) checks open() and pathlib-style calls, not `subprocess.run(..., text=True)` pipes. So a clean PLW1514 run does not show that subprocess output is decoded as UTF-8. The Approach and AC treat the ruff result as proof that the fix is complete without checking what the rule actually covers.
findings.location: Approach — PLW1514 bullet ('Done when `ruff check --preview --select PLW1514 src scripts` reports nothing'); Acceptance Criteria line 3
scenarios: On Windows, `git show --format=%B` output containing an em dash or non-Latin author name is decoded as cp1252 in verify_commit.py, producing mojibake or a UnicodeDecodeError, while PLW1514 reports clean.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider running the relevant unit tests (or a Linux CI step) with `PYTHONWARNDEFAULTENCODING=1 -W error::EncodingWarning` as the regression guard, instead of or alongside the ast scan of five modules, or say why the ast scan is preferred.
evidence: PEP 597 (retrieved): 'The -X warn_default_encoding option and the PYTHONWARNDEFAULTENCODING environment variable are added. They are used to enable EncodingWarning.'
CPython issue #100750 (retrieved): 'PEP 597: platform from_subprocess missing encoding kwarg' — EncodingWarning fires on subprocess text-mode calls that don't pass an encoding.
The plan already uses '`-X warn_default_encoding -W error::EncodingWarning`' for the hatch hook test, so the mechanism is known to the author.
findings.finding: The new ast-scan regression test checks only the five CLI-consumer modules for `encoding="utf-8"` next to `text=True`. Python already has a standard mechanism that detects this whole class at runtime: PEP 597's EncodingWarning, enabled with `-X warn_default_encoding` / `PYTHONWARNDEFAULTENCODING=1`. It also fires for subprocess text mode. The plan already uses this mechanism for the hatch-hook test, but doesn't consider it in place of, or alongside, the hand-written ast scan.
findings.location: Testing — 'an `ast` scan of the five CLI-consumer modules' bullet
scenarios: Someone later adds `subprocess.run(..., text=True)` without an encoding in a sixth module that shells out to the rebar CLI. The ast scan's fixed list of five modules misses it, and it only shows up on the advisory Windows sweep.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Linux CI/test step (or a pytest `filterwarnings = error::EncodingWarning` setting run under `PYTHONWARNDEFAULTENCODING=1`) covering the CLI-consumer and binding-repository tests. Keep the ast scan only if you want a static check that doesn't depend on which paths the tests actually execute.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a Linux proxy check: run the tests in `text-encoding.args` with `PYTHONWARNDEFAULTENCODING=1 PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 pytest -W error::EncodingWarning @.github/windows-sweep-deselect/text-encoding.args`, and require it to pass before removing lines.
evidence: "The 133 tests pass under `make verify`"
"The advisory `sweep (windows)` job deselects the 133 tests"
findings.finding: 'The 133 tests pass under `make verify`' proves nothing about the fix. These tests are deselected only on Windows and already pass on Linux. The plan names no Linux-side proxy that would reveal remaining locale-default I/O in the 133 tests before the Windows run.
findings.location: Testing (last line)
scenarios: A test in the list still calls `read_text()` without an encoding. It passes `make verify` on Linux and fails on Windows.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the `make verify` sentence with: 'the tests listed in text-encoding.args pass under `PYTHONWARNDEFAULTENCODING=1 PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 python -m pytest -W error::EncodingWarning @.github/windows-sweep-deselect/text-encoding.args`, and under `make verify`'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either move `_use_utf8_stdio()` to a shared helper and also call it at the top of `rebar.reconciler.__main__.main`, while adding `encoding="utf-8"` to `_bridge_runner._spawn_bounded`'s Popen (and covering it in the AST scan), or state explicitly that the reconciler entry point is out of scope and why.
evidence: src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py:128 `(sys.executable, "-m", "rebar.reconciler", ...)`; :140-150 Popen(... stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE, text=True, errors="replace") with no encoding
src/rebar/reconciler/__main__.py:114-149 `main()` installs the stderr handler and runs the pass without going through rebar._cli.main
Plan lists only `_cli/__init__.py` as the stdio fix point, and five consumer modules, none of which is `_bridge_runner.py`
findings.finding: The stdio fix lives only in `rebar._cli.main`, but rebar has a second entry point whose output is captured over a pipe: `python -m rebar.reconciler`. reconciler/__main__.py:114 has its own `main` that never calls `_cli.main`. `_bridge_runner._spawn_bounded` (:140-150) captures that child's stdout/stderr with `text=True, errors="replace"` and the locale codec. On Windows the reconciler child's piped stdio stays cp1252, which is the same root cause the plan names ('the CLI's stdio is cp1252'). That pair also does not meet the plan's rule that every rebar-output consumer names its encoding.
findings.location: Approach — `_use_utf8_stdio()` bullet and the 'Product parents that capture rebar CLI output' bullet; Scope
scenarios: Windows reconcile bridge: the reconciler prints a ticket title or diagnostic outside cp1252 → UnicodeEncodeError in the child; or, once only one side changes, the parent mis-decodes

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Run `gh workflow run test.yml --ref <pr-branch>` before merge and only remove args-file lines whose tests pass there; state that any line failing on main post-merge is restored in the args file.
evidence: "Remove each fixed line from `text-encoding.args`; delete the file and its `@` line ... once empty"
"Windows: `gh workflow run test.yml --ref main` after merge"
"Every line removed ... names a test that passed in a `sweep (windows)` run on main after the fix"
findings.finding: The plan removes lines from `text-encoding.args` (and possibly deletes the file and its `@` line) in the PR before merge. Proof that those tests pass on Windows comes only from `gh workflow run test.yml --ref main` after merge. No pre-merge Windows run is planned, and there is no recovery step if the post-merge run fails.
findings.location: Approach (last bullet) / Testing (last line) / AC 4–5
scenarios: A test still does locale-default I/O on Windows. It is removed from the args file, and the main sweep goes red after merge with no planned back-out.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a pre-merge step: dispatch the sweep on the PR branch and remove only lines that passed there. Add a back-out rule: if the post-merge main run fails, re-add the failing ids to `text-encoding.args`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State what the CLI-consumer parents surface when child output is not valid UTF-8, and make it hold: set PYTHONUTF8=1 in the child env and/or use `errors="replace"` on capture.
evidence: "Product parents that capture rebar CLI output in text mode decode UTF-8 (`encoding="utf-8"`): `reconciler/pass_support.py:225`, `reconciler/run_differs.py:132`, ..."
"a new `_use_utf8_stdio()` called first in `main` (`:306`)" — output emitted before `main` (interpreter or import errors) is not covered.
Absence: no `errors=` choice or child `env` (e.g. PYTHONUTF8=1 / PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8) is specified for these parents.
findings.finding: The five product parents now strictly UTF-8-decode captured output from the rebar CLI child, stderr included. The child's stdio is only switched to UTF-8 once `main` runs. Anything the interpreter writes to stderr before that, such as an import-time traceback, is still in the locale codec. The parent's own `subprocess.run` then raises UnicodeDecodeError instead of surfacing the child's failure. The plan does not say what the parent surfaces in this case.
findings.location: Approach — 'Product parents that capture rebar CLI output in text mode decode UTF-8' bullet
scenarios: Windows, user profile `C:\Users\José\...`: the child fails at import, and Python writes a traceback containing the path to stderr in cp1252 (é = 0xE9). The reconciler parent raises UnicodeDecodeError while decoding stderr and loses the child's real error.
findings.suggested_fix: In each of the five parents, pass `env={**os.environ, "PYTHONUTF8": "1"}` (or PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8) to the child alongside `encoding="utf-8"`, and use `errors="replace"` for captured stderr so the child's failure is always reported.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Run `gh workflow run test.yml --ref <branch>` before merge and remove only deselect lines whose tests pass in that run; keep the post-merge main run as confirmation.
evidence: "Windows: `gh workflow run test.yml --ref main` after merge."
"Every line removed from `text-encoding.args` names a test that passed in a `sweep (windows)` run on main after the fix"
findings.finding: Lines are removed from `text-encoding.args` in the change itself, on the strength of Linux-simulated tests. Windows evidence comes only from a post-merge `gh workflow run ... --ref main`. Any of the 133 tests that still fails on Windows lands on main un-deselected, and the AC 'sweep (windows) concludes success' can only be checked after merge.
findings.location: Testing — 'Windows: `gh workflow run test.yml --ref main` after merge'; Acceptance Criteria lines 4–5
scenarios: One deselected test depends on a site the plan missed. The deselect line is removed, the post-merge Windows sweep fails on main, and a follow-up change is needed.
findings.suggested_fix: Dispatch the workflow on the feature branch before merging, prune `text-encoding.args` to the lines that passed there, and record that run id alongside the post-merge main run id.
